title: Helios Console — Access
description: RBAC and destructive-capability configuration for the Helios Console macOS app. Preference domain MUST be com.herojoneslabs.helios.console.access — deploy as its own Jamf Pro Application & Custom Settings profile, SCOPED TO ADMIN MACS ONLY (never to all managed Macs). FAIL-CLOSED GUARANTEE: a Mac that does NOT receive this profile runs as role=User — the destructive Cleanup feature is hidden and the default device-action allow-list applies — so under-scoping is safe; over-scoping is not. PAIRED SCOPING: a profile from this schema that grants role=Admin must be scoped to the same Macs as any write-capable variant of the com.herojoneslabs.helios.console.credentials profile (see docs/ConfigProfileMigration.md). SECURITY: managed-preference plists are world-readable on disk — every value delivered here is visible to any local user of the Mac.

configurationVersion.title: Configuration Version
configurationVersion.description: Schema/profile version stamp (informational — the app logs it, nothing else reads it).

role.title: Operator Role
role.description: Role-based access control. The destructive Cleanup feature is shown ONLY when this is exactly "Admin"; Support, User, blank, missing, or a typo all hide it (fail-closed). There is deliberately NO default: a Mac that never receives this profile stays at role=User. Scope this profile so only intended admins receive role=Admin.

cleanup.title: Cleanup (Stale Device) Settings
cleanup.description: Defaults for the Admin-only Cleanup feature. staleDays is the DEFAULT stale threshold; users can change it in-app unless you re-deliver this profile to reset it.

staleDays.title: Stale Threshold (days)
staleDays.description: Days without check-in before a device counts as stale. Deliver as an integer; the app also tolerates a string value (e.g. "90") because some deployed profiles ship it that way.

defaultStaticGroupID.title: Default Static Group ID
defaultStaticGroupID.description: Jamf static group ID pre-selected for Cleanup runs. Delivered as a string; parsed to an integer downstream.

defaultSiteID.title: Default Site ID
defaultSiteID.description: Jamf site ID pre-selected for Cleanup runs. Delivered as a string; parsed to an integer downstream.

deviceActions.title: Device Actions (allow-list)
deviceActions.description: STRICT FAIL-CLOSED per-action allow-list for the device Actions menu. If no actions array is delivered for a platform, that platform's Actions menu is HIDDEN ENTIRELY. If the array is present, ONLY listed actions with enabled=true are shown (and executable) — an id not listed, or listed with enabled=false, is hidden AND blocked at execution. Unknown ids are ignored (logged once) so newer profiles deploy safely to older app builds. The computer id "wipe" is now IMPLEMENTED — a bare erase (ERASE_DEVICE with recovery PIN) that ALWAYS waits for the device to acknowledge and keeps the Jamf record and Entra object; lock, viewRecoveryLockPassword, updateInventory, renewMDMProfile, sendCustomCommand, installPackage, and runPolicy remain reserved — granting them renders nothing. displayName overrides the menu label only. LEGACY: the app still decodes the pre-2.1 boolean-map shape (e.g. computer.restart=true) when no actions array is delivered — explicitly delivered keys become grants, and the old per-key defaults are no longer applied — but this schema (2.1+) exposes ONLY the actions array; computer/mobileDevice reject any other property, so profiles built or edited from this schema cannot reintroduce the old flat keys. Migrate deployed legacy profiles to the actions array. The core domain's jamfPro.screenShareEnabled key is DEPRECATED: once an allow-list is delivered it is authoritative for screenShare too.

displayName.title: Menu Label Override
displayName.description: Overrides the Actions-menu label ONLY. Confirmation-dialog safety copy is app-built-in and never profile-controlled. Empty = built-in label.

requiredTier.title: Required User Tier (Entra sign-in only)
requiredTier.description: Minimum signed-in user tier for this action — the USER-scoped layer 2 of a two-layer gate (the machine-scoped allow-list above must ALSO grant the action; both must allow). ACTIVE ONLY when the core domain sets signIn.method=entra; in email sign-in mode this key is ignored entirely, so existing deployments are unaffected. OMIT the key to use the action's built-in classification — Operator: sendBlankPush, enableBluetooth, disableBluetooth; Admin: restart, restartSilent, shutdown, wipe, returnToService, enableRemoteDesktop, disableRemoteDesktop, screenShare, viewLocalAdminPassword, viewFileVaultKey, unlockUserAccount (reserved ids — lock, updateInventory, viewRecoveryLockPassword, renewMDMProfile, sendCustomCommand, installPackage, runPolicy — render nothing regardless of tier). FAIL-CLOSED UPWARD: any delivered value other than exactly "Admin" or "Operator" (typo, wrong case, "None") is treated as Admin — a malformed value restricts, never expands. The Cleanup feature is NOT configurable here: it is gated by the core domain's signIn.entra.cleanupRoles role set (admin-tier users always qualify; listed roles extend the grant).

options.title: Action Options (Return to Service)
options.description: Consulted ONLY by the returnToService action; ignored for every other id. Both toggles default true, so omitting this object keeps the original full-decommission behavior. The erase always runs first and ALWAYS waits for the device to acknowledge ERASE_DEVICE — no cleanup step runs without that acknowledgment. deleteEntraObject auto-skips when Entra isn't configured.

deleteJamfRecord.title: Delete Jamf Pro Record
deleteJamfRecord.description: Remove the computer record from Jamf Pro after the erase is acknowledged.

deleteEntraObject.title: Delete Entra Device Object
deleteEntraObject.description: Delete the device object from Microsoft Entra after the erase is acknowledged, so the device can re-enroll cleanly.

mobileDevice.title: Mobile Device Actions
mobileDevice.description: Forward-looking: the mobile device detail view has no actions menu yet. Any future menu is built from this allow-list from day one.

displayName.title: Menu Label Override
displayName.description: Overrides the Actions-menu label ONLY. Confirmation-dialog safety copy is app-built-in and never profile-controlled. Empty = built-in label.

requiredTier.title: Required User Tier (Entra sign-in only)
requiredTier.description: Forward-looking — no mobile actions menu exists yet. Same semantics as the computer key when one ships: consulted only when signIn.method=entra; unknown values fail closed to Admin.
